Which one below was born first?
Maria Goeppert Mayer (born 1906) is the earliest of the four. In 1986, the Maria Goeppert Mayer Award for early-career women physicists was established in her honor.
Which of these four is the oldest?
Lisp (programming language) (founded 1958) is the earliest of the four.
Who among these is an astronomer?
Annie Jump Cannon is an astronomer.
Which of these is a mathematician?
Andrew Wiles is a mathematician. In 2018, Wiles was appointed the first Regius Professor of Mathematics at Oxford.
What is the atomic number of Plutonium?
Plutonium is a chemical element; it has symbol Pu and atomic number 94.
What is the atomic number of Rhenium?
Rhenium is a chemical element; it has symbol Re and atomic number 75.
In what year was Isaac Newton born?
Isaac Newton: Newton contributed to and refined the scientific method, and his work is considered the most influential in bringing forth modern science.
In what year was LSD discovered?
LSD taken orally has an onset of action of 0.4 to 1.0 hours and a duration of 7 to 12 hours.
TeX: Donald Knuth. TeX is a popular means of typesetting complex mathematical formulae; it has been noted as one of the most sophisticated digital typographical systems.
Tupolev Tu-204: Kazan Aircraft Production Association. It was developed for Aeroflot as a replacement for the medium-range Tupolev Tu-154 trijet in the 1990s.
HTML: United Kingdom. Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) is the standard markup language for documents designed to be displayed in a web browser.
Who is credited with discovering Moscovium?
Moscovium: Joint Institute for Nuclear Research. Moscovium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Mc and atomic number 115.
Who is credited with discovering Oxycodone?
Oxycodone: Martin Freund. It is a highly addictive and commonly abused drug.
Who is credited with discovering Germanium?
Germanium: Clemens Winkler. Germanium is a chemical element; it has the symbol Ge and atomic number 32.
Bred for strength and endurance to haul heavy loads across the snow, this large sled-dog breed shares its arctic heritage with breeds like the Siberian Husky and Samoyed — what breed is it?
Alaskan Malamute is a large breed of dog that was originally bred for its strength and endurance to haul heavy freight as a sled dog.
Famed for foundational work in number theory and algebraic geometry, this French mathematician was also a principal founder of the secretive Bourbaki group — who was he?
André Weil (6 May 1906 - 6 August 1998) was a French mathematician, known for his foundational work in number theory and algebraic geometry.
This deciduous shrub genus in the rose family comes in black, red, and hybrid purple berry varieties, all bitter enough to usually be processed rather than eaten fresh — which genus?
Aronia is a genus of deciduous shrubs, the chokeberries, in the family Rosaceae native to eastern North America and most commonly found in wet woods and swamps.
These nocturnal blood-feeding insects from the genus Cimex can trigger skin rashes, itching, and even psychological distress from their bites — what are they commonly called?
Bed bug are insects from the genus Cimex, which are parasites that feed on blood, usually at night.
Native to North America and introduced to Europe in the 1930s, these prostrate shrubs in the genus Vaccinium range from 4 inches to 13 feet tall — what fruit is it?
Blueberry are a widely distributed and widespread group of perennial flowering plants with blue or purple berries.
Which winged insect fluttered into the fossil record around 56 million years ago and reaches adulthood only after pupating inside a chrysalis?

Butterfly are winged insects from the lepidopteran superfamily Papilionoidea, characterised by large, often brightly coloured wings that often fold together when at rest, and a conspicuous, fluttering flight.
Combining science, aesthetics, and technique, this field is the study and practice of making and using maps to communicate spatial information — what field is it?

Cartography is the study and practice of making and using maps. The fundamental objectives of traditional cartography are to:

Set the map's agenda and select traits of the object to be mapped.
Made of DNA wound around histone proteins, this substance shapes chromosomes into their distinctive forms during cell division and gatekeeps access to genes for transcription and repair — what is it?
Chromatin is a complex of DNA and protein responsible for condensing and packaging chromosomal DNA.
Known in the US as 'konk,' this sea snail's family includes so-called 'true' species identified by their long spires — what is it?
Conch is any of a number of different medium-to-large-sized sea snails.
Unrelated to poor hygiene, this scalp condition causes flaking and mild itching and is often treated with antifungal or keratolytic remedies; about half of all adults experience it. What is it?
Dandruff is a skin condition of the scalp. It can result in social or self-esteem problems.
Native to western North America, this towering conifer is also nicknamed Oregon pine or Columbian pine, though it isn't truly a pine at all — which tree?
Douglas fir (Pseudotsuga menziesii) is an evergreen conifer species in the pine family, Pinaceae.
Tissue similar to the uterine lining grows elsewhere in the body—often on the ovaries, fallopian tubes, or pelvis—affecting roughly 10% of women of reproductive age worldwide. What is this condition?
Endometriosis is a disease in which tissue similar to the endometrium - the lining of the uterus (womb) - grows elsewhere in the body.

This suborder of meat-eating mammals groups together the 'cat-like' carnivorans — cats, hyenas, mongooses, and viverrids — in contrast to their 'dog-like' counterparts in the other major suborder. What suborder is this?
Feliformia is a suborder within the order Carnivora consisting of "cat-like" carnivorans, including cats, hyenas, mongooses, viverrids, and related taxa.
Often bonded to glucose to form table sugar, this white, water-soluble simple sugar occurs naturally in honey, tree and vine fruits, and most root vegetables — name this sugar?
Fructose is a common monosaccharide, i.e.

Found in northern South America, this tarantula is the world's heaviest and longest-bodied spider, tipping the scales at over 170 grams, though a huntsman spider still beats it on leg span — what spider is it?
Goliath birdeater (Theraphosa blondi) is a large spider that belongs to the tarantula family Theraphosidae.
This usually benign tumor made of blood vessels typically appears on a baby's skin at birth or within weeks, often on the face, scalp, chest, or back, then shrinks over childhood — what is it?
Hemangioma is a usually benign vascular tumor derived from blood vessel cell types.
Sold as a 3 percent solution for the bathroom cabinet but explosive when concentrated, this oxidizer and antiseptic carries the formula H2O2 — what is it?
Hydrogen peroxide is a chemical compound with the formula H2O2.
This flowering plant genus boasts 310 species with showy blooms, some known by the common name 'flags' and a horticultural subgroup called 'junos' — what genus is it?
Iris (plant) is a flowering plant genus of 310 accepted species with showy flowers.

A civil engineer who commanded the Australian Corps in 1918, this WWI general was called by historian A. J. P. Taylor 'the only general of creative originality produced by the First World War' — who was he?
John Monash (27 June 1865 - 8 October 1931) was an Australian military commander of the First World War and a civil engineer.

Named after a French mathematician but reportedly learned from his Swiss tutor, this calculus theorem evaluates tricky limits by taking derivatives of the numerator and denominator — what is it called?
L'Hôpital's rule (loh-pee-TAHL) is a mathematical theorem used for evaluating the limit of a quotient of two functions, each of which tends to zero or infinity, by taking each function's derivative.
This common, soft, movable, painless growth made of fatty tissue usually forms just under the skin, often on the back, shoulders, or abdomen — name this benign tumor?
Lipoma is a benign tumor made of fat tissue. The first use of the term "lipoma" to describe these tumors was in 1709.

Located partly outside the body and partly within the pelvis, this set of sex organs includes the testicles, which produce sperm to fertilize an egg during conception — which body system is being described?
Male reproductive system consists of a number of sex organs that play a role in the process of human reproduction.
A waxy crystalline compound from peppermint and corn mint, it triggers a cooling sensation and works as a mild local anesthetic to soothe a sore throat — what is it?
Menthol is a monoterpenoid organic compound that occurs naturally in the oils of certain plants in the mint family, such as corn mint and peppermint.
Classified by carbon count into trioses, pentoses, hexoses, and more, these colorless, water-soluble simple sugars are the basic building blocks of carbohydrates — what are they called?
Monosaccharide (from Greek monos: single, sacchar: sugar), also called simple sugars, are a class of organic compounds usually with the formula (CH2O)x.
Composed of a renal corpuscle and a renal tubule, this microscopic structural and functional unit of the kidney numbers between 1 and 1.5 million per healthy adult kidney — name it?

Nephron is the minute or microscopic structural and functional unit of the kidney. The renal corpuscle consists of a tuft of capillaries called a glomerulus and a cup-shaped structure called Bowman's capsule.
Yellowing, thickening, and a nail separating from its bed are telltale signs of this fungal infection, far more common in toenails than fingernails — what's the medical name?
Onychomycosis is a fungal infection of the nail. Onychomycosis, also known as tinea unguium, is a fungal infection of the nail.
Combining medicine with comedy, this physician organizes volunteers to clown around for orphans and patients worldwide through a nonprofit institute he founded in 1989 — who is he?
Patch Adams (born May 28, 1945) is an American physician, comedian, social activist, clown, and author.
This bird genus, part of the flamingo family Phoenicopteridae, encompasses the living flamingo species — which genus?
Phoenicopterus is a genus of birds in the flamingo family Phoenicopteridae.

First domesticated by ancient peoples of the Iranian plateau roughly 5,000 years ago, this deciduous shrub bears a fruit rich in symbolic and mythological meaning across many cultures — name the fruit?
Pomegranate (Punica granatum) is a fruit-bearing, deciduous shrub in the family Lythraceae, subfamily Punicoideae, that grows to between 1.5-5 metres (5-16 ft) tall.
Like a cosmic lighthouse, this highly magnetized, rapidly rotating neutron star is only visible from Earth when its beam of radiation sweeps directly toward us — what's the object?
Pulsar (pulsating star, on the model of quasar) is a highly magnetized rotating neutron star that emits beams of electromagnetic radiation out of its magnetic poles.

One of the rarest and most valuable precious metals, this hard, corrosion-resistant transition metal with only one naturally occurring isotope is prized for enhancing jewelry — what's the element (symbol Rh, atomic number 45)?
Rhodium is a chemical element; it has symbol Rh and atomic number 45.
Arising from connective tissues like bone, cartilage, muscle, and fat, this rare cancer of mesenchymal cells makes up just 1% of adult diagnoses but 15% of childhood ones. What is it?
Sarcoma is a rare type of cancer that arises from cells of mesenchymal origin.
Despite its long-nosed, mouse-like look, this small mammal is actually a closer cousin to hedgehogs and moles than to rodents — what is it?
Shrew (family Soricidae) are small mole-like mammals classified in the order Eulipotyphla.
Doctors examine the color of this coughed-up airway mucus — greenish or yellow tints can hint at infection, though not which organism caused it — what is it?
Sputum is mucus that is coughed up from the lower airways (the trachea and bronchi).
This Polish far-right entrepreneur and tax advisor placed third in the 2025 presidential election while chairing a libertarian party and co-leading a far-right coalition — who is he?
Sławomir Mentzen (born 20 November 1986) is a Polish far-right politician, entrepreneur and tax advisor.
A parasitic arachnid roughly 3 to 5 millimeters long that feeds on the blood of mammals and birds, with fossils dating back some 100 million years to the Cretaceous — which creature?
Tick are parasitic arachnids of the order Ixodida.
This broad category of large, hoofed mammals was reclassified in 2001 into a new clade after genetic data revealed the older grouping wasn't a true evolutionary lineage. Name the category of animals?
Ungulate are members of the diverse clade Euungulata, which primarily consists of large mammals with hooves.
This German hunting-dog breed, recognized in 1891, is so much a working dog that in its homeland it's considered unsuitable simply as a house pet — name the breed?
Weimaraner is a German breed of hunting dog of medium to large size, with history going back at least to the nineteenth century.

Unlike a user interface, which links a computer to a person, this software connection lets programs talk directly to each other — and the standard describing it is called its specification. What's the three-letter term?
API: Connection between computers or programs.
Nicknamed the 'killer' variety for its aggressive defense of the hive, this hybrid pollinating insect escaped Brazilian quarantine in 1957 and reached Texas by 1990 — which insect is it?
Africanized bee: Hybrid species of bee. The African honey bee was first introduced to Brazil in 1956 to increase honey production, but 26 swarms escaped quarantine in 1957.
Also called ramsons or bear leek, this bulbous woodland plant native to Eurasia is a wild cousin of onion and garlic — what is it?
Allium ursinum: Species of flowering plant in the family Amaryllidaceae.
Comprising more than 140 species across 16 genera, this small, oily forage fish is found everywhere from the Atlantic to the Black Sea — what is it?
Also known as Umbelliferae and including carrots, celery, parsley, and dill, this plant family also contains dangerously toxic members like poison hemlock and giant hogweed — which family?

One of its founders, James Keeler, said this science 'seeks to ascertain the nature of the heavenly bodies... rather than their positions or motions' — studying everything from the Sun to the cosmic microwave background. What field is it?
A tender herb of the mint family native from Central Africa to Southeast Asia, its Genovese or 'sweet' variety is a kitchen staple worldwide — what is it?
Basil: Culinary herb. Basil (Ocimum basilicum), also called great basil, is a culinary herb of the family Lamiaceae (mints).

Closely related to the beech-oak family and including species widespread across the Northern Hemisphere's temperate and boreal zones, which thin-leaved deciduous hardwood genus is prized for its versatile wood?
Birch: Genus of flowering plants in the family Betulaceae.
This highly venomous snake in the Colubridae family, scientifically known as Dispholidus typus, is native to Sub-Saharan Africa — what is its common name?
One of the largest snake species on Earth, this Southeast Asian native became invasive in Florida after escaping the pet trade — which snake is this?
Burmese python: Species of large, nonvenomous snake.
Its Latin name means 'horned goat,' and it's often pictured as a half-goat, half-fish sea creature — which is the smallest constellation of the zodiac?
Capricornus: Zodiac constellation in the southern hemisphere.

Nicknamed the 'solar' web for its sunburst of radiating nerve fibers, this abdominal structure sits behind the stomach and in front of the diaphragm's crura, near where several major arteries branch off the aorta — what is it?
Celiac plexus: Complex network of nerves located in the upper abdomen.

Caused by a bacterium and often symptomless for weeks after exposure, this sexually transmitted infection can lead to pelvic inflammatory disease and infertility in women if untreated — which infection?
Chlamydia: Sexually transmitted bacterial infection. Chlamydia, or more specifically a chlamydia infection, is a sexually transmitted infection caused by the bacterium Chlamydia trachomatis.
Striking at the same hour every day for weeks at a time, usually around one eye, this excruciating neurological condition is considered one of the most painful known to medicine — what is it?
Cluster headache: Neurological disorder. The disease is considered among the most painful conditions known to medical science.

Native to Europe and North Africa, this member of the carrot family can grow to 8 feet tall, with hollow stems blotched dark maroon and a distinctly foul smell carried on the wind — which highly poisonous plant is this?
Conium maculatum: Poisonous plant. The plant is herbaceous, with no woody parts, and has a biennial lifecycle.
A creeping vine of the gourd family that originated across India, Nepal, and southern China, this plant comes in slicing, pickling, and seedless types — what is it?
Cucumber: Species of flowering plant with edible fruits.

This acute medical syndrome develops over hours or days and causes disturbed attention, awareness, and sometimes hallucinations — often triggered by illness, substances, or their withdrawal — what is it called?
Delirium: Severe confusion that develops quickly, and often fluctuates in intensity.
A dentist and gambler who fought alongside lawman Wyatt Earp at the O.K. Corral, his reputation claimed dozens of killings though researchers count just one to three — who was this gunfighter?
Doc Holliday: Gambler, gunfighter, and dentist in the American West (1851–1887)
After stints at the CIA, Dell, and Booz Allen Hamilton, this NSA contractor flew to Hong Kong in 2013 and leaked thousands of classified documents exposing global surveillance — who is he?
Edward Snowden: Whistleblower and NSA contractor (born 1983)
One of the four basic animal tissue types, this thin protective cell layer lines blood vessels and body cavities and includes the skin's outer layer — what is it called?
Epithelium: Tissue lining the surfaces of organs in animals.
In this small bird of prey, females can be up to 25% larger than males — one of the biggest size gaps between sexes of any bird — and it hunts garden songbirds across Europe and Asia — which raptor?

Eurasian sparrowhawk: Species of bird. The Eurasian sparrowhawk (Accipiter nisus), also known as the northern sparrowhawk or simply the sparrowhawk, is a small bird of prey in the family Accipitridae.
Marketed under brand names like Allegra, this second-generation antihistamine treats allergy symptoms without crossing the blood-brain barrier the way older drugs do — what medication is it?
Fexofenadine: Antihistamine medication. Fexofenadine is an antihistamine medication used in the treatment of allergy symptoms such as allergic rhinitis and urticaria.
Dead at just 26, this British thinker had already reshaped philosophy, mathematics and economics — and as an undergraduate translated Wittgenstein's 'Tractatus' into English; who was he?
Frank P. Ramsey: British philosopher, mathematician and economist (1903–1930)
With a siphon that can stretch over three feet and a shell just 6 to 8 inches across, this giant Pacific burrowing clam can live up to 179 years — which creature?
Caused by the bacterium Neisseria gonorrhoeae and colloquially called 'the clap,' this sexually transmitted infection can pass from mother to child during birth — what is it?
Gonorrhea: Sexually transmitted infection. Gonorrhea or gonorrhoea, colloquially known as the clap, is a sexually transmitted infection (STI) caused by the bacterium Neisseria gonorrhoeae.
This standard markup language structures web documents using elements delineated by tags, often paired with CSS and JavaScript — what is it?
HTML: Markup language for documents. Hypertext Markup Language (HTML) is the standard markup language for documents designed to be displayed in a web browser.
This inflammation of the liver can cause jaundice and, if it becomes chronic, progress to cirrhosis — most commonly caused by five different viruses labeled A through E. What condition is it?
Hepatitis: Inflammation of the liver. Hepatitis is acute if it resolves within six months, and chronic if it lasts longer than six months.
The most widespread of all primates, this bipedal, nearly hairless species owes its advanced technology, culture, and language to a large, complex brain — what is it?
Human: Species of hominid in the genus Homo.
Typically starting to work within an hour, this NSAID relieves pain, fever, and inflammation but can worsen asthma and, in later pregnancy, is considered harmful — which drug?

Credited with the oldest known systematic classification of chemical substances, this alchemist's corpus also contains the earliest instructions for deriving ammonium chloride from organic matter — who is he?
Jabir ibn Hayyan: Islamic alchemist and polymath (died c. 806–816)
This British physicist shared the 1951 Nobel Prize with Ernest Walton for first splitting the atomic nucleus — a feat that opened the way to nuclear power and weapons. Who was he?
Patented in 1967 and approved for medical use in 1980, this propionic-acid-class NSAID works by blocking prostaglandin production — what is it?
The last member of the actinide series, this synthetic element honors the man who invented the cyclotron — the very machine used to discover so many artificial elements. Which element is it?
Lawrencium: Chemical element with atomic number 103 (Lr)
Understood before 1950 purely as the ability to decode written words, this concept later expanded to include the social and cultural dimensions of reading and writing — what skill is it?
Literacy: Ability to read and write.
Found in the hundreds inside most animal cells but almost never in plant cells, this acidic, enzyme-packed organelle serves as the cell's degradation center — which organelle?
Lysosome: Cell membrane organelle. A lysosome (/ˈlaɪsəˌsoʊm/) is a membrane-bound organelle that is found in all animal cells (except red blood cells), and rarely in plant cells.

The first woman to win a Nobel Prize and the first person to win two, this Polish-born physicist and chemist discovered revolutionary elements and shared groundbreaking research on radioactivity with her husband—making her one of history's most influential scientists. Who was she?
Marie Curie: Polish-French physicist and chemist (1867–1934)
Nicknamed 'meow meow' and chemically related to compounds in the khat plant, this synthetic stimulant produces effects similar to MDMA and was first synthesized in 1929 — which drug?
Mephedrone: Recreational drug. Mephedrone, also known as 4-methylmethcathinone, 4-MMC, or 4-methylephedrone, is a synthetic stimulant drug belonging to the amphetamine and cathinone classes.

Codenamed 'Havoc' by NATO, this Soviet tandem-seat attack helicopter carries a single gun in an under-nose barbette and, unlike its predecessor, has no secondary troop-transport role. What aircraft is this?
Mil Mi-28: Russian attack helicopter. The Mil Mi-28 (NATO reporting name "Havoc") is a Soviet heavy-weight, all-weather, day-night, tandem-seat anti-armour military attack helicopter.
Numbering roughly 160,000 species and mostly active at night, these insects share an order with butterflies but are known for their duller, darker wings — what are they?
Moth: Group of mostly-nocturnal insects in the order Lepidoptera.
Also called the belly button, this flat or hollowed spot on the abdomen marks where the umbilical cord once attached — what is it?
Navel: Scarred area on the abdomen after detachment of the umbilical cord.

As the United States' first swept-wing fighter jet, this Korean War-era aircraft dueled Soviet MiG-15s in some of history's earliest jet-to-jet battles — which plane, produced in more than 7,800 units?
North American F-86 Sabre: Family of US fighter aircraft.
The most arboreal of the great apes, with long arms, short legs and reddish-brown hair, this genus Pongo primate survives today only in the rainforests of Borneo and Sumatra — what is it?
Orangutan: Genus of Asian apes. The most arboreal of the great apes, orangutans spend most of their time in trees.

Named for its resemblance to a related crested dinosaur, this duck-billed herbivore could grow over 9 meters long, moved on two or four legs, and was first described in 1922 by William Parks — which dinosaur genus?
Parasaurolophus: Hadrosaurid ornithopod dinosaur genus from Late Cretaceous Period.
Created by Larry Wall in 1987 as a Unix scripting tool for report processing, this language's planned sixth version was eventually spun off and renamed Raku — which programming language?
Perl: Interpreted programming language first released in 1987.
Resembling a round, tailless rabbit with short ears, this small mountain-dwelling mammal's Himalayan relative lives at elevations above 6,000 meters — what animal is it?
Pika: Genus of mountain-dwelling mammal. A pika ( PY-kə, PEE-kə) is a small, mountain-dwelling mammal native to Asia and North America.
This succulent plant in the family Portulacaceae has every part edible, whether raw or cooked, and is also known by folk names like little hogweed — what is it, scientifically speaking?
Portulaca oleracea: Species of plant in the purslane family.

This noncontagious autoimmune disease shows up as dry, scaly red or purple patches, and injuring the skin can trigger new lesions right at that spot — a quirk called the Koebner phenomenon — what is it?
Psoriasis: Autoimmune diseases of the skin. Psoriasis is a long-lasting, noncontagious autoimmune disease characterized by patches of abnormal skin.

Born Richard Alpert, this spiritual teacher researched psychedelics with Timothy Leary at Harvard before writing the 1971 bestseller Be Here Now, popularizing Eastern spirituality in the West. What name did he later take?
As chairman of Purdue Pharma, this physician-businessman oversaw the launch of OxyContin and was later portrayed in the miniseries Dopesick and Painkiller — who is he?

Formed by the fusion of five vertebrae between the ages of 18 and 30, this triangular bone sits at the base of the spine and connects to the tailbone below and the last lumbar vertebra above. What is it?
Sacrum: Bone of the spine. The sacrum situates at the upper, back part of the pelvic cavity, between the two wings of the pelvis.
Covered in a spiny shell called a test and moving via tiny tube feet, this globular ocean-floor animal grazes mostly on algae — what creature is it?
Sea urchin: Class of marine invertebrates.

This primate group includes every animal traditionally called a monkey or ape — including humans — and split from the tarsiers roughly 60 million years ago. What's the term for this broader classification?
Also called dinkel wheat, this high-protein relict crop has been a staple in parts of Europe since the Bronze Age and is considered a hexaploid hybrid of common wheat and emmer — what is it?
Spelt: Species of wheat. It is a relict crop, eaten in Central Europe and northern Spain.

This speech disorder involves involuntary repetitions and prolongations of sounds or words, affects roughly 1% of the world's population, and is unrelated to a person's ability to structure their thoughts — what's it called?
Stuttering: Speech disorder. Persistent stuttering into adulthood often leads to outcomes detrimental to overall mental health, such as social isolation and suicidal thoughts.
Pig-shaped with a short, flexible snout, this odd-toed ungulate mammal lives in the jungles of South and Central America and Southeast Asia, alongside equine and rhino relatives — which animal?
Covered in sharp spikes along its leaf margins to ward off herbivores, this prickly flowering plant's fluffy seed head is known as 'down.' What is it?
Thistle: Common name of a group of flowering plants.
Sold as Tramal, this opioid painkiller doubles as an SNRI — which means it carries a rare risk of serotonin syndrome. What is it?
This hypothetical element 126, nicknamed eka-plutonium, intrigues physicists because 126 may be a 'magic number' of protons sitting near the center of a predicted island of stability — what is it?
Unbihexium: Theoretical chemical element with atomic number 126 (Ubh)
This chronic autoimmune disorder causes patches of skin to lose their pigment, and in antiquity it was so misunderstood that it was often confused with leprosy — what is it?
Vitiligo: Skin condition where patches lose pigment.
A short evergreen shrub with dull green leaves and orange-red berries, this nightshade-family plant is better known by names like Indian ginseng and winter cherry — what is it?
Withania somnifera: Species of flowering plant.
The symbol for silicon is Si. Silicon is a chemical element; it has symbol Si and atomic number 14.
The symbol for fermium is Fm. Fermium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Fm and atomic number 100.

A Man Called Otto: A Man Called Otto is a 2022 American comedy-drama film directed by Marc Forster from a screenplay by David Magee.
